# Naṅguṭṭhajātaka (Ja 144)
**ID:** Ja 144
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Naṅguṭṭhajātaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja144
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Naṅguṭṭhajātaka* (Ja 144) is a canonical Jātaka tale set at Jetavana, delivered by the Buddha concerning the erroneous austerities (*micchātapa*) of naked Ājīvika ascetics, such as squatting penances (*ukkuṭikappadhāna*) and bat-vows (*vaggulivata*) [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877]. Its opening canonical verse begins with the phrase *Bahum pe taṁ asabbhi jātaveda* [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877].
In the story of the past, the Bodhisatta is offered a choice by his parents to either renounce the world or become a householder who masters the three Vedas [Bronkhorst 1998]. Living as an ascetic tending the sacred fire of Agni (Jātaveda), he prepares to sacrifice a bull; however, while he steps away to a nearby village to procure salt, hunters come upon the sacrifice, consume all the meat, and leave behind only the bull's tail [von Glasenapp 1966]. Repulsed by the god's inability to preserve his own offering, the Bodhisatta quenches the sacrificial fire with water, takes up the ascetic life of a seer (*isipabbajjā*), attains the higher spiritual knowledges (*abhiññā*) and meditative absorptions (*samāpatti*), and is ultimately reborn in the Brahmā world [Fausböll 1877; Bronkhorst 1998]. Helmuth von Glasenapp highlights this tale as an example of the dissociation of the god concept from its natural substrate [von Glasenapp 1966], while Johannes Bronkhorst notes its depiction of Vedic asceticism existing apart from Vedic textual study [Bronkhorst 1998].
SuttaCentral records no curated early parallels in other languages and lists four modern translations [SuttaCentral]. Machine-assisted alignment via DharmaNexus similarly detected no significant Pali-internal text reuse or cross-language matches scoring 10 or above [DharmaNexus].
